feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant leadership scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited quantified outcomes beyond traffic/platform scale.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, culminating in director-level leadership and then consulting; this strengthens credibility and narrative.  
- Strong domain fit: web modernization, governance, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are consistently reinforced.  
- Good use of concrete scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which adds impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and the footer projects; consolidate to create a tighter structure and improve scanability.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: cost savings, engagement lifts, adoption rates, campaign performance, process efficiency, or stakeholder impact would strengthen results.  
- Fix style consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “front-end” vs. other hyphenation choices, and mixed punctuation/list formatting. Minor grammar/style edits: remove the comma in “web, email, social, and multimedia” if using a non-serial-comma style elsewhere; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler in Education. No obvious misspellings or major typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. Tightening it and adding one concrete scale cue would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, content, and analytics systems for high-volume public-sector organizations. Builds governance models, editorial operations, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences that improve publishing efficiency, discovery, and audience engagement.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more active, outcome-oriented language such as “modernizing,” “scaling,” or “leading.”
- Add a specific credibility marker from recent experience if space allows, e.g., “10,000+ page website” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Use parallel phrasing: “web modernization, analytics, governance, editorial systems, and multimedia operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Governance models and content operations” is repeated across the intro, competencies, and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and with slightly tighter, more executive-level wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more concise, parallel phrasing: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” for clearer meaning and stronger alignment with the AI search work.
- Consider “cross-channel” instead of “multi-channel” for a more current, polished tone.
- Keep this section focused on capability areas, not tools or outcomes, since those are covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization” and “AI-enabled search…” repeat language from the header almost verbatim.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills; consider trimming either section if space is tight.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in like “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a crisp one-line achievement with parallel structure.
- Replace generic verbs (“Built,” “Developed”) with stronger, more differentiated ones: “Launched,” “Led,” “Created,” “Delivered.”
- Clarify specificity where possible: e.g., “legislative search,” “Drupal 10 microsite,” “interactive conference display,” and “recurring advocacy video series” are good—add audience, scale, or purpose if space allows.
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the NACo roles; keep this section project-focused and avoid repeating responsibilities already stated above.
- “Editorial storytelling” and “production/distribution across website, email and social” echo existing experience bullets; emphasize distinct deliverables or outcomes instead.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with your NACo director role and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows and analytics to improve cross-team coordination,” “Built modular Drupal campaign experiences and member toolkits,” “Led AI search strategy spanning retrieval design, structured content, and UX.”
- Cut lower-value detail like “technical troubleshooting” unless tied to scale, speed, or reliability; combine CMS/front-end work into one concise bullet.
- Add 1–2 measurable outcomes if possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, publishing time reduced, engagement gains, search success metrics, or adoption across teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” repeats themes already covered in the 2022–2024 director role.
- Microsites/AI search also appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and reserve specifics/results for projects.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes while avoiding overlap with the adjacent NACo roles on newsletters, video, and day-to-day channel management.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope and leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, overseeing web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for the organization’s enterprise communications ecosystem.”
- Combine the website bullets and keep the strongest metrics: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes clearer on analytics/governance: add results such as faster reporting, improved decision-making cadence, reduced publishing inconsistency, or stronger cross-team adoption if you can quantify them.
- Reframe the studio bullet around organizational impact: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, expanding capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, systems, and transformation.
- Video-program language also appears in older NACo roles; emphasize building infrastructure, not producing recurring content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and quantify scope so it shows how this role built the foundation for the later director position.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Tighten bullets and lead with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Built cross-team editorial planning and standardized publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; use “managed” or “ran” here to preserve progression.
- Weekly video/update language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; emphasize scaling/formalizing rather than originating if that’s more accurate.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should sharpen the most senior, differentiated strengths and use tighter phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace with more specific, senior-level language:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content operations” or “web modernization,” which better reflects recent leadership scope.
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid broad phrases like “multi-channel communications leadership” unless paired with a clearer operational angle.
- If space allows, align this section more directly to recent impact areas: governance, modernization, analytics-informed strategy, and AI-enabled experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes rather than repeat a software list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as capability-led, not inventory-led; group tools under broader strengths.
- Suggested rewrite: **Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization and front-end implementation • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery**
- Remove “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” from this topline item; those fit better in Technical + IT.
- If accurate, strengthen with scope language tied to recent work, e.g. “enterprise CMS modernization” or “large-scale public-sector web platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies and recent project content; consider shortening here to “AI-enabled search.”
- Platform/tool names substantially repeat Technical + IT; avoid listing the same stack in both places.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic so it earns its place in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + tools: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization — GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic terms with stronger phrasing: change “KPI design” to “KPI framework development” and “Leadership reporting” to “Executive dashboarding and decision support”
- Tighten the final item: change “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX and content performance analysis”
- Optional full rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and content performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating every tool here if the Technical section already carries the full stack.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and several NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use sharper, more senior phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with leadership-oriented wording: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ camera and studio systems,” “Virtual event operations.”
- Consider a tighter version: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Drop “editing” unless it is a differentiator; “video production” already implies it.
- If possible, align with evidence from recent roles by adding scale elsewhere in the CV (e.g., studio buildout, recurring advocacy programming, event support volume).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.
- “Studio operations” and “video production” are already supported in recent NACo roles, so this skills line should stay concise rather than restating duties.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, without repeating the same tools elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light qualifiers to show level, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, governance)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented rather than just a list: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsite builds)** • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; if no notable GitHub Pages work appears elsewhere, consider dropping it for a stronger platform or version detail like **Drupal 10**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates Topline Skills [2]; consider trimming one or making this version more platform-specific and the other more capability-focused.
- “CMS modernization” is already covered elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless tied to a concrete platform outcome.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support your recent Drupal/AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context instead of only tools, e.g.: **Front-end development for Drupal-based sites, API-driven integrations, tag management, edge scripting, and deployment automation**
- Consider replacing older/generic terms with stronger signals of current use, e.g. move **jQuery** later in the list or qualify it as **legacy support** if that better reflects recent work

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one as a high-level summary and this one as the more technical/tool-specific version
- **API integrations** and technical execution themes also appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating identical wording across sections

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit
- Rename to emphasize capability, e.g. “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools.”
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier, then project/collaboration tools after.
- Group for clarity: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- If space allows, add light context instead of a pure list: “Used to build editorial workflows, intake systems, approvals and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Slack” and “Teams” are common workplace tools; keep only if you need keyword coverage.
- Since workflow automation already appears elsewhere, avoid repeating “workflow automation” verbatim in multiple sections unless this item is the only detailed tools list.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare relative to the rest of the CV. It would be stronger if it signaled level of use or business context, especially since email leadership already appears prominently in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email, CRM & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Replace with: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if these are tools you used directly and meaningfully.
- If space allows, add light qualifiers for credibility: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation) • Higher Logic (member communications) • Mailchimp (newsletter operations)**
- Put the most recent/enterprise-grade platform first; if Dynamics 365 is current or strategic, keep it first as listed.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and multi-channel communications; avoid adding outcome claims here unless they are not stated elsewhere.
- If Higher Logic or Mailchimp were only legacy/limited-use tools, consider dropping one to keep the list tighter and more senior.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and the NACo work bullets. Tighten it to emphasize methods/capabilities rather than repeating platforms already evidenced elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Experimentation & Reporting**
- Replace with a more capability-led line: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • dashboard development • SEO analysis**
- Drop **A/B testing** unless you can support it with a concrete project/result elsewhere; if retained, use **experiment design** for a more senior tone.
- Consider ordering by strongest/recent tools first: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity** then supporting capabilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item nearly duplicates the **Topline Skills: Analytics, Insights & Optimization** section; consider merging or making one tools-only and the other outcomes/capabilities-only.
- “Dashboarding” overlaps with reporting/infrastructure language already used in the 2022–2024 NACo role.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, site refresh support, and hands-on production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or process improvements.
- Tighten the close: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day oversight for a digital media associate.”
- If true, highlight a distinct contribution not repeated later: launch/standardization of livestream operations, early video program development, or foundational publishing processes.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or establishing the format here.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia” is similar to later governance/operations bullets; keep this more foundational and hands-on.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with one clear differentiator—the first podcast launch—but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize initiative, cross-functional coordination, and any concrete outputs.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo policy and program teams; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more active, specific line: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support member communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or outcomes: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so progression is clear; 1–2 lines is enough.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later video/multimedia entries; avoid repeating broad production language.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here since stronger leadership evidence appears in 2018–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps with stronger, higher-level multimedia language elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools/software here and leave production leadership to recent experience and Topline Skills.
